decisions.reason: As a very recent launch that was publicly highlighted as a new product line and fits the firm's stated move toward digital, connected practice workflows, management would be strongly inclined to continue backing it rather than withdraw after initial investment.

Because the education institute builds on the existing customer base and support capabilities, and there is no clear evidence of failure, management would likely justify its initial commitment by keeping it on the market.

The remote screen sharing support tool is closely tied to the firm's established service offering and efficient practice support strategy, so an escalation-of-commitment logic favors retaining it after development and rollout efforts.
